previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic pancreatitis and a history of recent candidemia from a central line was admitted with an acute flare characterized by severe epigastric pain radiating to the back, nausea, vomiting, and inability to tolerate oral intake. She was managed with bowel rest, IV fluids, and pain control using IV Dilaudid, a PCA pump, and transition to oral opioids. A PICC line was placed on 2170-09-06 to initiate TPN due to ongoing malnutrition and inability to eat. Right-sided back pain developed but resolved spontaneously with no evidence of renal infection. Migraine was treated with sumatriptan after Maxalt was unavailable. Her pancytopenia, including leukopenia and thrombocytopenia, remained stable and consistent with prior trends. Depression and GERD were managed with continued medications. She gradually improved, advanced to oral intake, and was discharged home with TPN, a PICC line, and plans for outpatient follow-up with nutrition support and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ year-old woman with h/o idiopathic 
chronic pancreatitis who comes with abdominal pain, nausea, and 
vomiting consistent with her chronic pancreatitis.

# Pancreatitis flare - Symptoms were consistent with her prior 
flares.  She was initially started on a dilaudid PCA, however 
she did not tolerate this well as she would fall asleep and not 
be able to administer her doses.  She was switched to IV 
dilaudid with good control of her pain.  The Pain service was 
consulted and they recommended increasing the gabapentin with a 
taper which was started.  She also got a dose of ketorolac which 
helped her pain as well.  She was weaned off the IV medications 
and had good control of her pain and nausea with her home PO 
regimen.

# Inactive Issues - The patients other medical problems were 
inactive and she was continued on her home regimen for 
depression, pain (with the exception of the gabapentin) and 
nausea.

Transitional Issues:
- Consideration of starting iron supplementation as the patient 
is iron deficient
- Uptitration of gabapentin - start 300mg morning dose, if 
tolerated for 5 days
would add 300 mg afternoon dose. (Would ultimately equal 300 am,
